pr.title: Replace the default branch with an unreachable branch If it is the last variant
pr.description:
Fixes #119520. Fixes #110097.

LLVM currently has limited ability to eliminate dead branches in switches, even with the patch of https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/issues/73446.

The main reasons are as follows:

- Additional costs are required to calculate the range of values, and there exist many scenarios that cannot be analyzed accurately.
- Matching values by bitwise calculation cannot handle odd branches, nor can it handle values like `-1, 0, 1`. See [SimplifyCFG.cpp#L5424](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/llvmorg-17.0.6/llvm/lib/Transforms/Utils/SimplifyCFG.cpp#L5424) and https://llvm.godbolt.org/z/qYMqhvMa8
- The current range information is continuous, even if the metadata for the range is submitted. See [ConstantRange.cpp#L1869-L1870](https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/blob/llvmorg-17.0.6/llvm/lib/IR/ConstantRange.cpp#L1869-L1870).
- The metadata of the range may be lost in passes such as SROA. See https://rust.godbolt.org/z/e7f87vKMK.

Although we can make improvements, I think it would be more appropriate to put this issue to rustc first. After all, we can easily know the possible values.

Note that we've currently found a slow compilation problem in the presence of unreachable branches. See 
https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/issues/78578.

r? compiler

issues.title: missed optimization for `if let`, even though equivalent match is optimized
issues.body:
<!--
Thank you for filing a bug report! 🐛 Please provide a short summary of the bug,
along with any information you feel relevant to replicating the bug.
-->

I tried this code:

```rust
pub fn change_value(val: Result<i32, ()>) -> Result<i32, ()> {
    if let Ok(x) = val {
        Ok(x * 2)
    } else {
        Err(())
    }
}

pub fn change_value2(val: Result<i32, ()>) -> Result<i32, ()> {
    match val {
        Ok(x) => Ok(x * 2),
        Err(()) => Err(())
    }
}
```

I expected to see this happen: 
in release build this code would translated into exact the same assembly/llvm-ir

Instead, this happened: 

```
change_value:
	xorl	%eax, %eax
	testl	%edi, %edi
	setne	%al
	leal	(%rsi,%rsi), %edx
	retq
change_value2:
	movl	%edi, %eax
	leal	(%rsi,%rsi), %edx
	retq
```

and the llvm-ir is different:

```
define { i32, i32 } @_ZN10playground12change_value17h0230bd4091fd6529E(i32 noundef %0, i32 %1) unnamed_addr #0 {
start:
  %2 = icmp eq i32 %0, 0
  %_4 = shl i32 %1, 1
  %not. = xor i1 %2, true
  %.sroa.0.0 = zext i1 %not. to i32
  %.sroa.3.0 = select i1 %2, i32 %_4, i32 undef
  %3 = insertvalue { i32, i32 } undef, i32 %.sroa.0.0, 0
  %4 = insertvalue { i32, i32 } %3, i32 %.sroa.3.0, 1
  ret { i32, i32 } %4
}
```

```
define { i32, i32 } @_ZN10playground13change_value217h3302fbc2853d0a41E(i32 noundef %0, i32 %1) unnamed_addr #0 {
start:
  %switch = icmp eq i32 %0, 0
  %_4 = shl i32 %1, 1
  %.sroa.3.0 = select i1 %switch, i32 %_4, i32 undef
  %2 = insertvalue { i32, i32 } undef, i32 %0, 0
  %3 = insertvalue { i32, i32 } %2, i32 %.sroa.3.0, 1
  ret { i32, i32 } %3
}
```

processing.reason: The PR's historical-vs-corrected change is purely an optimization of MIR shape: the old pass left the last allowed enum discriminant reachable through the SwitchInt `otherwise` edge, while the new pass adds that last variant explicitly and redirects `otherwise` to a fresh `unreachable` block. Both versions dispatch every valid discriminant to the same arm behavior, and neither version can be entered with an invalid/uninhabited discriminant without pre-existing UB. Therefore no defined concrete input can make the "original" and "incorrectly transformed" functions produce different numeric/boolean/character values, so a source-grounded semantic counterexample pair cannot be validated. The differing evidence is only later-pass elimination of a provably dead default branch (issues #119520/#110097) and a TailDuplicator compile-time workaround, not a runtime miscompilation.

analysis.summary: Extend UninhabitedEnumBranching so that when a SwitchInt over an enum discriminant has exactly one allowed variant left uncovered by explicit targets, that variant is added as an explicit target pointing at the current otherwise block, and the otherwise target (plus any uninhabited-value targets) is redirected to a fresh unreachable block. Encoding "the last valid discriminant" explicitly removes the live default edge, which is what allows later passes/LLVM to eliminate impossible enum branches (issues #119520, #110097). The final version also adds a successor heuristic to avoid a TailDuplicator compile-time blow-up.
analysis.originalLogic: The pass iterated SwitchInt terminators over an enum discriminant, computed `allowed_variants` from the enum layout (or from `discriminant_ty.variant_range(tcx)` when layout is unavailable), removed each explicit target value from that set and marked non-variant values for redirection to unreachable. It then only redirected the `otherwise` edge to unreachable when `reachable_count == allowed_variants.len()`, i.e. when every allowed variant already had an explicit target. If exactly one allowed variant remained reachable only through `otherwise`, the default edge stayed live. Source: "let allowed_variants = if let Ok(layout) = layout { variant_discriminants(&layout, discriminant_ty, tcx) } else ..."; "if reachable_count == allowed_variants.len() { removable_switchs.push((bb, targets.iter().count())); }".
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historical/old output: the pass left the remaining allowed discriminant merged into the `otherwise` edge, e.g. `switchInt(move _3) -> [0: bb3, 1: bb4, 2: bb2, otherwise: bb1]` with bb1 the live default, so later optimization/LLVM cannot prove the default branch impossible and cannot eliminate dead enum branches. The corrected transformation instead adds the last allowed variant explicitly to the old otherwise block and makes otherwise unreachable, e.g. `switchInt(move _3) -> [0: bb6, 1: bb6, 2: bb2, otherwise: bb6]` where bb6 is `unreachable;`. An intermediate historical implementation also applied the rewrite without checking the otherwise block's successors, which triggered the known TailDuplicator compile-time overhead ("we've currently found a slow compilation problem in the presence of unreachable branches"), fixed by the `check_successors` guard that declines to rewrite when the otherwise block's sole successor is another SwitchInt.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR functions containing `TerminatorKind::SwitchInt` on an enum discriminant where the discriminant type is known (layout available, or fall back to `discriminant_ty.variant_range(tcx)`), the `otherwise` block is a real non-empty-unreachable branch, and exactly one allowed enum variant is not already an explicit target. Includes simple enums, enums with uninhabited variants, custom/`#[repr(i8)]` discriminants with gaps and negative values, generic enums lacking layout, nested matches whose default branch is not directly a SwitchInt, and both panic=abort and panic=unwind strategies.
analysis.trigger: A SwitchInt over an enum discriminant whose `otherwise` block is not already an empty unreachable block and where `allowed_variants.len() == 1` after removing explicit target values (or `allowed_variants.is_empty()`); the final code computes a `replace_otherwise_to_unreachable` flag from `otherwise_is_last_variant || !otherwise_is_empty_unreachable && allowed_variants.is_empty()`. The successor guard additionally requires `check_successors(&body.basic_blocks, targets.otherwise())` to be true.
preconditions: The discriminant type's allowed variant set is known (layout via `variant_discriminants`, or fallback `discriminant_ty.variant_range(tcx)`); otherwise the pass must `continue` and not transform.
The `otherwise` block is not already `is_empty_unreachable()`, otherwise the rewrite is skipped.
After removing explicit target values from `allowed_variants`, exactly one variant remains (or none).

For the last-variant rewrite, the otherwise block's successor heuristic must pass: if the otherwise block has a single successor whose terminator is `SwitchInt`, do not rewrite (TailDuplicator compile-time workaround).
A dedicated non-cleanup unreachable block is used via `patch.unreachable_no_cleanup_block()` rather than sharing the cleanup unreachable block.
pitfalls: Redirecting `otherwise` to unreachable before adding an explicit target for the last allowed variant would send a valid discriminant to unreachable and miscompile; `targets.add_target(last_variant, targets.otherwise())` must capture the old otherwise target first.
`SwitchTargets::add_target` requires the value not already be present; the loop removes matched values from `allowed_variants` so only the truly remaining variant is added.
Reusing one unreachable block for both cleanup and non-cleanup edges is incorrect; the patch introduces `unreachable_no_cleanup_block` distinct from `unreachable_cleanup_block`.
Applying the rewrite unconditionally when `otherwise` is already empty unreachable creates redundant blocks and extra MIR churn; guard with `!otherwise_is_empty_unreachable`.
Without the `check_successors` guard (otherwise's sole successor is another `SwitchInt`), the rewrite causes TailDuplicator compile-time overhead, as documented by the LLVM issue 78578 comment.
Custom discriminants and generic enums may lack layout; use `variant_range`/`discriminant_for_variant` fallback so cases like `#[repr(i8)]` enums with `-1, 0, 5, 3` are still handled.
The rewrite changes only the default edge, not the semantics of the matched arms; tests must compare actual target values, not merely older diff fragments or comments.
analysis.testStrategy: Add MIR tests under tests/mir-opt with `//@ unit-test: UninhabitedEnumBranching` and `// EMIT_MIR_FOR_EACH_PANIC_STRATEGY`, checking with CHECK patterns that the switch's otherwise points to a dedicated `unreachable` block, e.g. `// CHECK: switchInt(move [[discr]]) -> [0: bb5, 1: bb5, 2: bb1, otherwise: [[unreachable:bb.*]]];` and `// CHECK: [[unreachable]]: { // CHECK-NEXT: unreachable;`. Cover the positive case (exactly one remaining variant), the non-transform case where otherwise is not empty unreachable and last variant not uniquely determined (`otherwise_t4`, `otherwise_t3`), the already-unreachable case, uninhabited default, custom discriminants, generic enums with no layout (`Test5<T>` with `#[repr(i8)]` explicit values), and the successor-is-SwitchInt guard. Add a codegen test `tests/codegen/enum/uninhabited_enum_default_branch.rs` with `-O` asserting the range/equality form (`add`, `icmp ult`, `icmp eq`, `or`, `ret`) to show the dead default disappeared. Also inspect downstream GVN/SimplifyLocals/JumpThreading diff updates, but note these only reflect the new explicit target/unreachable edge and do not establish correctness by themselves.
evidence: Replace the default branch with an unreachable branch If it is the last variant
LLVM currently has limited ability to eliminate dead branches in switches, even with the patch of https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project/issues/73446.
After all, we can easily know the possible values.
Note that we've currently found a slow compilation problem in the presence of unreachable branches.
